answer: Each agent stakes a unique hardware-backed cipher key, and every epoch the network samples a random subset to solve a lightweight proof tied to that key. Mapping agents to distinct keys via a public atlas of registrations prevents mass-created identities, since duplicating a key triggers slashing. A single whisper of collusion between clones is enough to flag the cluster and freeze rewards, making a sybil farm cost more in lost stake than it can receive.
